pages.title: Start with a Working Tier 1
pages.text: $(bold)1.$() Place the Energy Core controller at the intended center. Leave room around it; a future tier 8 shell occupies 13×13×13.$(br2)$(bold)2.$() Open the controller and select tier 1. Tier 1 needs no shell at all—the controller itself is the complete core body. It still needs four stabilizers before activation.

pages.title: Let the Controller Build It
pages.text: $(bold)3.$() For tier 2 or above, select the target tier, check the material lists later in this entry, and carry every required shell block in inventory. Press $(bold)Assemble Core$().$(br2)The controller consumes the matching materials and places the shell automatically; there is no need to place it block by block.

pages.title: What Auto-Assembly Omits
pages.text: If the shell remains incomplete, replenish the missing material, clear any obstructing blocks, and press $(bold)Assemble Core$() again. Use $(bold)Build Guide$() only to inspect remaining positions or build manually.$(br2)Assemble Core builds only the shell. The stabilizer structures and Energy Pylon must still be built separately.

pages.title: Place Four Stabilizers
pages.text: $(bold)4.$() Choose one axis to leave unused; the vertical axis is simplest. On the controller's level, place one Energy Core Stabilizer due north, south, east, and west.$(br2)Each must lie on a straight line from the controller, 1–15 blocks center-to-center, and outside the shell. The next diagram uses four blocks, suitable for tiers 1–4.

pages.name: Tier 1–4 Stabilizers
pages.text: Top view: four standalone stabilizers, each four blocks from the controller. Purple marks the real Energy Core controller; do not place glass. All four stabilizers must be on this same horizontal plane.

pages.title: Validate, Activate, Connect
pages.text: $(bold)5.$() Reopen the controller. Neither red warning—$(thing)Core Invalid$() nor $(thing)Stabilizers Invalid$()—should remain; then press $(bold)Activate$().$(br2)$(bold)6.$() Place an Energy Pylon near the active core and put one full glass block directly against any pylon face. Sneak-use the formed pylon to choose input or output, then connect the energy network to the pylon—not the controller.

pages.title: If Activation Is Refused
pages.text: $(bold)Core invalid:$() confirm the selected tier and every guide position; remove stray blocks where the guide expects air.$(br)$(bold)Stabilizers invalid:$() use exactly four centers, on four opposite directions around one shared axis, no farther than 15 blocks.$(br2)Tiers 5–8 require each center to expand into the nine-block 3×3 plane shown in $(l:draconic_insight:energy_storage/stabilizers_and_pylons)Stabilizers and Pylons$().

pages.title: Measurements, Tiers 1–4
pages.text: Material counts below exclude the controller and four stabilizers:$(br2)$(bold)Tier 1:$() controller only.$(br)$(bold)Tier 2 (3³):$() 6 Draconium Blocks.$(br)$(bold)Tier 3 (3³):$() 26 Draconium Blocks.$(br)$(bold)Tier 4 (5³):$() 54 Draconium Blocks and 26 Redstone Blocks.

pages.title: Measurements, Tiers 5–8
pages.text: These shell counts also exclude the controller and 36 advanced stabilizer blocks:$(br2)$(bold)Tier 5 (7³):$() 90 Draconium and 80 Redstone Blocks.$(br)$(bold)Tier 6 (9³):$() 150 Draconium and 178 Redstone Blocks.$(br)$(bold)Tier 7 (11³):$() 210 Draconium and 328 Redstone Blocks.$(br)$(bold)Tier 8 (13³):$() 786 Draconium and 378 Awakened Draconium Blocks.$(br2)Use the controller's guide for placement.

pages.name: Tier 1 Core
pages.text: Tier 1 is only the controller. The purple glass is ink for a visible marker, not a block to place—put the actual Energy Core controller there.

pages.name: Tier 2 Core
pages.text: Tier 2 places one Draconium Block on every face of the controller. Purple marks the real controller; do not build it from glass.

pages.name: Tier 3 Core
pages.text: Tier 3 is a solid 3×3×3 Draconium cube except for the true controller at its center, shown here by the purple marker.

pages.name: Tier 4 Core
pages.text: Tier 4 adds a Redstone interior and Draconium shell. Purple is only a drawn marker for the real controller—never place glass there. Trust the controller's guide for exact placement.
